## 1:7/q03 How does 'those who' work grammatically and morphologically?  [ٱلَّذِينَ · grammar]
- 1:7/q03/p1 Genitive ghayri is an adjective of alladhīna, not of the pronoun in ʿalayhim; its definite annexation permits this description because neither expression denotes a specified person. — FARRA: Genitive ghayri is an adjective of alladhīna, not of the pronoun in ʿalayhim; its definite annexation permits this description because neither expression denotes a specified person. [1 notes: FARRA]
- 1:7/q03/p2 Ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim is accusative as an appositive to al-ṣirāṭ. — AKHFASH: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim is accusative as an appositive to al-ṣirāṭ. [1 notes: AKHFASH]
- 1:7/q03/p3 Apposition is better than the adjective analysis because alladhī and alladhīna remain definite; he argues that rajul mithluka is generic, while Zayd mithluka only works as apposition. — AKHFASH: Apposition is better than the adjective analysis because alladhī and alladhīna remain definite; he argues that rajul mithluka is generic, while Zayd mithluka only works as apposition. [1 notes: AKHFASH+]

- 1:7/q03/p16 They read sirat man anʿamta ʿalayhim instead of sirat alladhina anʿamta ʿalayhim. — MAWARDI-FULL reporting عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير: They read sirat man anʿamta ʿalayhim instead of sirat alladhina anʿamta ʿalayhim. [1 notes: MAWARDI-FULL(عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير)]
- 1:7/q03/p17 Ṣirāṭ in ṣirāṭ alladhīna is an appositive restating the first ṣirāṭ in meaning, like calling one's father by the name Zayd. — WAHIDI-BASIT: Ṣirāṭ in ṣirāṭ alladhīna is an appositive restating the first ṣirāṭ in meaning, like calling one's father by the name Zayd. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p18 Relative pronouns such as alladhī and alladhīna are incomplete until their clause supplies a predicate, verb, circumstance, or conditional structure; that clause must contain a pronoun referring back. — WAHIDI-BASIT: Relative pronouns such as alladhī and alladhīna are incomplete until their clause supplies a predicate, verb, circumstance, or conditional structure; that clause must contain a pronoun referring back. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p19 Alladhīna is indeclinable across nominative, accusative, and genitive because it remains incomplete without its relative clause and thus resembles a particle. — WAHIDI-BASIT: Alladhīna is indeclinable across nominative, accusative, and genitive because it remains incomplete without its relative clause and thus resembles a particle. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p20 Abū Isḥāq, following Sībawayh, al-Khalīl, and al-Akhfash, says the original form of alladhī was ladh on the faʿl pattern. — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting أبو إسحاق: Abū Isḥāq, following Sībawayh, al-Khalīl, and al-Akhfash, says the original form of alladhī was ladh on the faʿl pattern. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT(أبو إسحاق)]
- 1:7/q03/p21 Abū al-Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī says the alif and lām in alladhī and related forms are fixed additions: other relatives such as man, mā, and ayy are definite without them, and the relative clause itself identifies alladhī. — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting أبو الفتح الموصلي: Abū al-Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī says the alif and lām in alladhī and related forms are fixed additions: other relatives such as man, mā, and ayy are definite without them, and the relative clause itself identifies alladhī. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT(أبو الفتح الموصلي)]
- 1:7/q03/p22 The added lām is retained because alladhī enables a clause to describe a definite noun: ordinary clauses are indefinite, and the particle alif-lām cannot attach directly to a clause. — WAHIDI-BASIT: The added lām is retained because alladhī enables a clause to describe a definite noun: ordinary clauses are indefinite, and the particle alif-lām cannot attach directly to a clause. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p23 Alladhī turns the sentence into a relative clause and marks the description as definite, as in the construction Zayd alladhī abūhu munṭaliq. — WAHIDI-BASIT: Alladhī turns the sentence into a relative clause and marks the description as definite, as in the construction Zayd alladhī abūhu munṭaliq. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p24 In the verse, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim means the road of those on whom You bestowed favor; the clause could describe an indefinite qawm directly, but not a definite group. — WAHIDI-BASIT: In the verse, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim means the road of those on whom You bestowed favor; the clause could describe an indefinite qawm directly, but not a definite group. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p25 Ghayr can be genitive as an appositive to alladhīna or as its adjective; the adjective is valid because the relative phrase here is not a particular, singled-out group. — WAHIDI-BASIT: Ghayr can be genitive as an appositive to alladhīna or as its adjective; the adjective is valid because the relative phrase here is not a particular, singled-out group. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q03/p26 As an adjective, ghayr can modify alladhīna here only because the relative phrase does not single out a particular group, making it like an indefinite description. — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting صاحب الحجة: As an adjective, ghayr can modify alladhīna here only because the relative phrase does not single out a particular group, making it like an indefinite description. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT(صاحب الحجة)]
- 1:7/q03/p27 In al-Fātiḥa, ṣirāṭ is the object, al-mustaqīm its adjective, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim apposes the preceding phrase, and the remaining clauses modify or coordinate with it. — JURJANI-DALAIL: In al-Fātiḥa, ṣirāṭ is the object, al-mustaqīm its adjective, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim apposes the preceding phrase, and the remaining clauses modify or coordinate with it. [1 notes: JURJANI-DALAIL]
- 1:7/q03/p28 Sirat alladhina is appositive to the straight path and repeats the request for guidance. — KASHSHAF: Sirat alladhina is appositive to the straight path and repeats the request for guidance. [1 notes: KASHSHAF]
- 1:7/q03/p29 Ibn Masud reads the phrase as the path of those whom You blessed, using a relative pronoun instead of alladhina. — KASHSHAF-FULL reporting ابن مسعود: Ibn Masud reads the phrase as the path of those whom You blessed, using a relative pronoun instead of alladhina. [1 notes: KASHSHAF-FULL(ابن مسعود)]
- 1:7/q03/p30 Ghayr can qualify the definite phrase because alladhina is not temporally delimited and the contrary identities of the two groups remove its ambiguity; it can also be accusative as a circumstantial phrase. — KASHSHAF-FULL: Ghayr can qualify the definite phrase because alladhina is not temporally delimited and the contrary identities of the two groups remove its ambiguity; it can also be accusative as a circumstantial phrase. [1 notes: KASHSHAF-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p31 The relative plural derives from لذٍ; its yāʾ drops with nunation and returns when the definite article is prefixed. — IBNATIYYA: The relative plural derives from لذٍ; its yāʾ drops with nunation and returns when the definite article is prefixed. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA]
- 1:7/q03/p32 On the genitive reading, ghayr can be an appositive to الذين or an adjective to an indefinite, since الذين here is not specifically singled out. — IBNATIYYA reporting أبو علي: On the genitive reading, ghayr can be an appositive to الذين or an adjective to an indefinite, since الذين here is not specifically singled out. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q03/p33 He explains that Ibn al-Sarrāj preserves الذين as definite and permits a definite adjective, while others treat ghayr as indefinite and approximate الذين to a general noun. — IBNATIYYA: He explains that Ibn al-Sarrāj preserves الذين as definite and permits a definite adjective, while others treat ghayr as indefinite and approximate الذين to a general noun. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA]
- 1:7/q03/p34 Makkī says lā prevents readers from mistaking the astray for a coordinate of الذين. — IBNATIYYA reporting مكي: Makkī says lā prevents readers from mistaking the astray for a coordinate of الذين. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA(مكي)]
- 1:7/q03/p35 Alladhina is the plural of alladhi; its yāʾ is removed in the indefinite form but restored with the article, and its plural may also be declined by some Arabs. — IBNATIYYA-FULL: Alladhina is the plural of alladhi; its yāʾ is removed in the indefinite form but restored with the article, and its plural may also be declined by some Arabs. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p36 Abu ʿAli explains jarr as either an appositive for alladhina or an adjective of an indefinite expression, since alladhina here is not used to specify particular people. — IBNATIYYA-FULL reporting أبو علي: Abu ʿAli explains jarr as either an appositive for alladhina or an adjective of an indefinite expression, since alladhina here is not used to specify particular people. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA-FULL(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q03/p37 Abu Bakr keeps alladhina definite and allows ghayr to describe it because context makes ghayr definite; other grammarians treat alladhina as a common, near-indefinite term and allow an indefinite adjective. — IBNATIYYA-FULL: Abu Bakr keeps alladhina definite and allows ghayr to describe it because context makes ghayr definite; other grammarians treat alladhina as a common, near-indefinite term and allow an indefinite adjective. [1 notes: IBNATIYYA-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p38 Ṣirāṭ alladhīna is either an adjective of al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm or its apposition; apposition implies repeating the syntactic governor, unlike an adjective.; cited verses: 7:75 — TABRISI: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna is either an adjective of al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm or its apposition; apposition implies repeating the syntactic governor, unlike an adjective. | mentions 7:75 [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q03/p39 Alladhīna is a relative noun, and anʿamta ʿalayhim is its relative clause; together they form a genitive noun annexed to ṣirāṭ. — TABRISI: Alladhīna is a relative noun, and anʿamta ʿalayhim is its relative clause; together they form a genitive noun annexed to ṣirāṭ. [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q03/p40 In the genitive, ghayr may be an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim or to alladhīna, or an adjective of the relative phrase despite ghayr usually modifying an indefinite noun. — TABRISI: In the genitive, ghayr may be an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim or to alladhīna, or an adjective of the relative phrase despite ghayr usually modifying an indefinite noun. [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q03/p41 Al-Zajjaj allows ghayr as an adjective of alladhīna because the relative phrase does not target named individuals, much like a generic man like you. — TABRISI reporting الزجاج: Al-Zajjaj allows ghayr as an adjective of alladhīna because the relative phrase does not target named individuals, much like a generic man like you. [1 notes: TABRISI(الزجاج)]
- 1:7/q03/p42 Al-Rummani allows the adjective because alladhīna with its clause functions like a common noun rather than a proper name. — TABRISI reporting علي بن عيسى الرماني: Al-Rummani allows the adjective because alladhīna with its clause functions like a common noun rather than a proper name. [1 notes: TABRISI(علي بن عيسى الرماني)]
- 1:7/q03/p43 Qur'anic usage has alladhina in three cases; Hudhayl has nominative alladhun, and other Arabs use alladhu or alladhi. — QURTUBI: Qur'anic usage has alladhina in three cases; Hudhayl has nominative alladhun, and other Arabs use alladhu or alladhi. [1 notes: QURTUBI]
- 1:7/q03/p44 Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr read “the path of whom You favored,” using man instead of alladhina. — QURTUBI reporting عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير: Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr read “the path of whom You favored,” using man instead of alladhina. [1 notes: QURTUBI(عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير)]
- 1:7/q03/p45 The genitive may make ghayr an appositive to alladhina or to the pronoun in alayhim, or an adjective; although definite nouns usually are not modified by indefinite ones, alladhina is general here or ghayr is definite between… — QURTUBI-FULL: The genitive may make ghayr an appositive to alladhina or to the pronoun in alayhim, or an adjective; although definite nouns usually are not modified by indefinite ones, alladhina is general here or ghayr is definite between exclusive opposites. [1 notes: QURTUBI-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p46 Although ghayr normally does not become definite through annexation, it can modify the definite alladhina here: between opposites it takes definiteness, and both terms are generic yet partly specified, balancing their ambiguity and particularity. — NASAFI: Although ghayr normally does not become definite through annexation, it can modify the definite alladhina here: between opposites it takes definiteness, and both terms are generic yet partly specified, balancing their ambiguity and particularity. [1 notes: NASAFI]
- 1:7/q03/p47 The relative pronoun الذين is most eloquently declined with yāʾ in all three cases, though some Arabs use wāw in the nominative; dropping its nūn is permitted, though some restrict that to poetic necessity. — ABUHAYYAN: The relative pronoun الذين is most eloquently declined with yāʾ in all three cases, though some Arabs use wāw in the nominative; dropping its nūn is permitted, though some restrict that to poetic necessity. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q03/p48 Grammarians disagree about how الذين is recognized; unlike الذي, it is restricted to rational beings. — ABUHAYYAN: Grammarians disagree about how الذين is recognized; unlike الذي, it is restricted to rational beings. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q03/p49 Al-Hasan and al-Dahhāk read صراطاً مستقيماً without the definite article; صراط الذين then apposes a definite expression to an indefinite one, as in 42:52.; cited verses: 42:52 — ABUHAYYAN reporting الحسن والضحاك: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhāk read صراطاً مستقيماً without the definite article; صراط الذين then apposes a definite expression to an indefinite one, as in 42:52. | mentions 42:52 [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN(الحسن والضحاك)]
- 1:7/q03/p50 Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads صراط مستقيم with an annexation, meaning the upright religion; with this and the majority reading, صراط الذين is a clarifying apposition of one definite expression to another. — ABUHAYYAN reporting جعفر الصادق: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads صراط مستقيم with an annexation, meaning the upright religion; with this and the majority reading, صراط الذين is a clarifying apposition of one definite expression to another. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN(جعفر الصادق)]
- 1:7/q03/p51 Abū ʿAlī parses genitive ghayr as an apposition either to الذين or to the pronoun in عليهم; Abū Ḥayyān calls both analyses weak because apposition by an adjective is weak. — ABUHAYYAN reporting أبو علي: Abū ʿAlī parses genitive ghayr as an apposition either to الذين or to the pronoun in عليهم; Abū Ḥayyān calls both analyses weak because apposition by an adjective is weak. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q03/p52 Al-Mahdawī and others parse accusative ghayr as a circumstantial accusative from عليهم, or from الذين; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the latter because the genitive complement has no syntactic position for a circumstantial modifier. — ABUHAYYAN reporting المهدوي: Al-Mahdawī and others parse accusative ghayr as a circumstantial accusative from عليهم, or from الذين; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the latter because the genitive complement has no syntactic position for a circumstantial modifier. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN(المهدوي)]
- 1:7/q03/p53 Lā reinforces the negation already contained in ghayr and is attached to المغضوب عليهم to avoid suggesting that الضالين is coordinated with الذين. — ABUHAYYAN: Lā reinforces the negation already contained in ghayr and is attached to المغضوب عليهم to avoid suggesting that الضالين is coordinated with الذين. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q03/p54 The relative clause of الذين uses a past verb to make God's favor definite and established; the clause with أل uses a participle encompassing all times, and makes the anger passive rather than directly ascribing it to… — ABUHAYYAN: The relative clause of الذين uses a past verb to make God's favor definite and established; the clause with أل uses a participle encompassing all times, and makes the anger passive rather than directly ascribing it to God. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q03/p55 Abū Ḥayyān concludes that the sūra is seven verses by consensus apart from disregarded dissent; Meccan and Kufan counters differ over whether the basmala or صراط الذين is an āya, while ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd counts eight and… — ABUHAYYAN: Abū Ḥayyān concludes that the sūra is seven verses by consensus apart from disregarded dissent; Meccan and Kufan counters differ over whether the basmala or صراط الذين is an āya, while ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd counts eight and Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī six. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q03/p56 Alladhīna is a relative pronoun, usually yāʾ in every case but sometimes wāw in the nominative; it refers to rational beings, unlike alladhī. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: Alladhīna is a relative pronoun, usually yāʾ in every case but sometimes wāw in the nominative; it refers to rational beings, unlike alladhī. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p57 Deleting the nūn of the relative pronoun is allowed, though some grammarians restrict it to poetic necessity unless it is not for specification. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: Deleting the nūn of the relative pronoun is allowed, though some grammarians restrict it to poetic necessity unless it is not for specification. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p58 Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read “the path of those whom You favored” without the relative pronoun. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL reporting ابن مسعود: Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read “the path of those whom You favored” without the relative pronoun. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL(ابن مسعود)]
- 1:7/q03/p59 Putting favor in the verbal relative clause of “those” fixes it to an established act, while the participial “incurred anger” leaves its time broad; the past verb specifies confirmed favor. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: Putting favor in the verbal relative clause of “those” fixes it to an established act, while the participial “incurred anger” leaves its time broad; the past verb specifies confirmed favor. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q03/p60 Alladhīna is genitive through annexation, a relative plural requiring a clause and resumptive; it usually has yāʾ in all cases, though some raise it with wāw, as in the cited verse. — SAMIN-DURR: Alladhīna is genitive through annexation, a relative plural requiring a clause and resumptive; it usually has yāʾ in all cases, though some raise it with wāw, as in the cited verse. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p61 A poetic form uses alladhūna with nominative wāw, and another deletes the relative's nūn to lengthen its clause; the plural is restricted to rational beings unlike singular alladhī. — SAMIN-DURR: A poetic form uses alladhūna with nominative wāw, and another deletes the relative's nūn to lengthen its clause; the plural is restricted to rational beings unlike singular alladhī. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p62 Anʿamta is the relative clause: tāʾ is its attached nominative second-person subject, and ʿalayhim is governed by the verb and supplies the resumptive pronoun. — SAMIN-DURR: Anʿamta is the relative clause: tāʾ is its attached nominative second-person subject, and ʿalayhim is governed by the verb and supplies the resumptive pronoun. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p63 Ghayr is an indefinite apposition to alladhīna; calling it an adjective is difficult because ghayr is indefinite and the relative is definite. — SAMIN-DURR: Ghayr is an indefinite apposition to alladhīna; calling it an adjective is difficult because ghayr is indefinite and the relative is definite. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p64 Makkī says ghayr replaces the attached pronoun in ʿalayhim; the author objects that deleting the replaced pronoun would leave the relative clause without its resumptive. — SAMIN-DURR reporting مكي: Makkī says ghayr replaces the attached pronoun in ʿalayhim; the author objects that deleting the replaced pronoun would leave the relative clause without its resumptive. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR(مكي)]
- 1:7/q03/p65 Ghayr is also read in the accusative as a circumstantial from alladhīna or ʿalayhim, or as a disjoint exception; al-Farrāʾ rejects the latter because lā lacks a preceding negation. — SAMIN-DURR: Ghayr is also read in the accusative as a circumstantial from alladhīna or ʿalayhim, or as a disjoint exception; al-Farrāʾ rejects the latter because lā lacks a preceding negation. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p66 The past-tense relative clause presents God's blessing as established, while the noun after al generalizes across times; passive wording tactfully avoids attributing anger directly to the deity. — SAMIN-DURR: The past-tense relative clause presents God's blessing as established, while the noun after al generalizes across times; passive wording tactfully avoids attributing anger directly to the deity. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p67 Ṣirāṭ alladhīna is a complete apposition, a definite noun replacing another definite noun. — SAMIN-DURR: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna is a complete apposition, a definite noun replacing another definite noun. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
- 1:7/q03/p68 In الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم, غضب is the single opposite of blessing: the first group is believers and the second disbelievers. — BURHAN: In الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم, غضب is the single opposite of blessing: the first group is believers and the second disbelievers. - 1:7/q03/p70 Stopping after these phrases is good because their sense is understood, but starting with attached phrases such as rabb al-ʿālamīn, ṣirāṭ alladhīna, or ghayr al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim is poor, except at verse ends per the Sunnah. — NASHR: Stopping after these phrases is good because their sense is understood, but starting with attached phrases such as rabb al-ʿālamīn, ṣirāṭ alladhīna, or ghayr al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim is poor, except at verse ends per the Sunnah. [1 notes: NASHR]
- 1:7/q03/p71 Stopping deliberately at ghayr or alladhīna is unanimously forbidden because the first is in construct and the second is connected; Sajawandi's lā forbids beginning there, not stopping before it. — NASHR: Stopping deliberately at ghayr or alladhīna is unanimously forbidden because the first is in construct and the second is connected; Sajawandi's lā forbids beginning there, not stopping before it. [1 notes: NASHR]
- 1:7/q03/p72 Ghayr is a matching apposition to alladhīna. Making it an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim is semantically awkward; the relative clause still contains its pronoun because the antecedent is not truly discarded. — ALUSI: Ghayr is a matching apposition to alladhīna. - 1:7/q03/p74 The objection from 35:37 does not disprove this definiteness: ṣāliḥan may be a fronted circumstantial accusative, or ghayr alladhī may be an apposition to it.; cited verses: 35:37 — ALUSI: The objection from 35:37 does not disprove this definiteness: ṣāliḥan may be a fronted circumstantial accusative, or ghayr alladhī may be an apposition to it. | mentions 35:37 [1 notes: ALUSI]
- 1:7/q03/p75 “Other than those who incurred anger” is a complete appositive for “those whom You favored”; taking it as an appositive for their pronoun is semantically awkward, though the relative clause remains grammatically attached. — ALUSI-FULL: “Other than those who incurred anger” is a complete appositive for “those whom You favored”; taking it as an appositive for their pronoun is semantically awkward, though the relative clause remains grammatically attached. [1 notes: ALUSI-FULL]

[1 notes: IBNASHUR-FULL]

## 1:7/q04 Who are those whom God favored?  [ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ · referent]
turns on: Whether the words include every obedient recipient of guidance or single out prophets, believers, earlier communities, or the Prophet's circle; 4:69 is repeatedly cited.
- 1:7/q04/p1 Believers or Muslims — TAB reporting ابن عباس: Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report through Ibn Jurayj, identifies the favored as believers. TAB reporting وكيع: Wakīʿ identifies the favored as Muslims. IBNABIHATIM reporting مجاهد: Mujahid identifies those favored as the believers. SULAMI reporting ابن عطاء: The blessed are knowers granted knowledge, saints granted sincerity, contentment, and certainty, the righteous granted patience and compassion, seekers granted obedience's sweetness, and believers granted steadfastness. MAWARDI-FULL reporting وكيع: He identifies those favored as Muslims. KASHSHAF: Those blessed are the believers. KASHSHAF-FULL: Those blessed are believers, and the wording leaves blessing general because Islam gathers every blessing. IBNATIYYA-FULL reporting ابن عباس: Another statement from Ibn ʿAbbas says the favored are believers. RAZI-FULL: The verse divides people into the obedient who are favored, sinners under wrath, and those ignorant of religion or unbelievers who are astray. NASAFI-FULL: “The path of those You favored” is an appositive restating the straight path, both reinforcing the point and identifying it as the Muslims' path; this emphatically attests to its uprightness. ABUHAYYAN reporting وكيع: Wakīʿ identifies those favored as Muslims. IBNKATHIR reporting وكيع: Wakiʿ identifies those favored as Muslims. BURSEVI: Calling the path that of people God favored, rather than people killed or punished, softens the demand and invites believers toward prophetic and saintly states. ALUSI reporting قيل: One view identifies those blessed as believers in general. TABATABAI reporting علي: Ali says the blessed are those favored with success in religion and obedience, not merely wealth or health, since disbelievers and sinners may also enjoy those worldly gifts. | mentions 4:69 [15 notes: TAB(ابن عباس,وكيع); IBNABIHATIM(مجاهد); SULAMI(ابن عطاء); MAWARDI-FULL(وكيع); KASHSHAF; KASHSHAF-FULL; IBNATIYYA-FULL(ابن عباس); RAZI-FULL; NASAFI-FULL; ABUHAYYAN(وكيع); IBNKATHIR(وكيع); BURSEVI; ALUSI(قيل); TABATABAI(علي)]
- 1:7/q04/p2 Prophets — MUQATIL: Those granted favor are the prophets, whom God favored with prophethood. | mentions 19:58 TAB reporting الربيع: Al-Rabīʿ says the favored are the prophets. TAB reporting عبد الرحمن بن زيد: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says the favored are the Prophet and those with him. MAWARDI reporting unattributed: Another view identifies those favored as the prophets. DAMGHANI: Niʿmah can mean prophethood, as in the people favored with prophecy. | mentions 4:69, 93:11 BAGHAWI-FULL reporting عكرمة: Ikrima says those favored were granted guidance and steadfastness in faith and right conduct, and identifies them as the prophets. BAYDAWI: One interpretation identifies those blessed with the prophets. IBNKATHIR reporting الربيع بن أنس: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, through Abu Jaʿfar, identifies those favored as the prophets. DURR reporting قتادة: In Qatada's sequential gloss, the Day of Recompense is when creatures are repaid; the worship-prayer is what people should say and directs them to God; the straight path is named, the favored are prophets, the objects of anger are Jews, and the astray are Christians. DURR reporting أبو زيد: Abū Zayd identifies those favored as the Prophet and those with him. DURR reporting الربيع بن أنس: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas identifies the favored as prophets, those under wrath as Jews, and the astray as Christians. DURR-FULL reporting الربيع بن أنس: Al-Rabi ibn Anas identifies the favored as prophets, those under anger as Jews, and the astray as Christians. IBNASHUR-FULL: The favored are recipients of complete blessing, especially earlier messengers and prophets; substitution shows that guidance itself is a blessing and the fully blessed were guided. IBNASHUR-FULL: Whether the favored are prophets, their best followers, or earlier Muslims, the prayer asks for complete guidance as appropriate to each era's attained and un attained guidance. ASAD-NOTES: The blessed are those given prophetic guidance and enabled to benefit from it. SAMARRAI-LAMASAT: A present-tense blessing would omit the earlier prophets and righteous, imply no established past recipients, and obscure continuity in one path from Adam onward. [16 notes: MUQATIL; TAB(الربيع,عبد الرحمن بن زيد); MAWARDI(unattributed); DAMGHANI; BAGHAWI-FULL(عكرمة); BAYDAWI; IBNKATHIR(الربيع بن أنس); DURR(أبو زيد,الربيع بن أنس,قتادة); DURR-FULL(الربيع بن أنس); IBNASHUR-FULL; ASAD-NOTES; SAMARRAI-LAMASAT]
- 1:7/q04/p3 Prophets, truthful people, martyrs, righteous people, and sometimes angels and all obedient worshippers — TAB reporting ابن عباس: Ibn ʿAbbās, transmitted through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, identifies the favored as obedient worshippers among the angels, prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous. TAB-FULL reporting ابن عباس: Ibn Abbas says those favored include obedient worshippers among angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous. IBNABIHATIM reporting ابن عباس: Ibn Abbas identifies those favored as obedient angels, prophets, truthful ones, and martyrs who worshipped God. MAWARDI-FULL: Those favored are variously identified as angels, prophets, believers in earlier scriptures, Muslims, or Muhammad and his Companions. TABRISI: The favored people are those who obey God and the Messenger, as identified in the verse listing prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous. | mentions 4:69 IBNJAWZI-ZAD reporting ابن عباس: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those favored by God as the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous. RAZI-FULL: The verse means asking for the path of those favored; 4:69 identifies them as prophets and the truthful, whose chief is Abu Bakr, so it supports his imamate and the propriety of following him. | mentions 4:69 DURR reporting ابن عباس: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the favored path as that of obedient worshippers among angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous. DURR-FULL reporting ابن عباس: Ibn Abbas identifies those favored as obedient angels, prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people. TABATABAI: The blessed are those who obey God and the Messenger: prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people, described by complete outward and inward submission. | mentions 4:69, 4:65, 4:66 SAMARRAI-LAMASAT: The past tense in You blessed identifies established recipients, including prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people. | mentions 4:69 [11 notes: TAB(ابن عباس); TAB-FULL(ابن عباس); IBNABIHATIM(ابن عباس); MAWARDI-FULL; TABRISI; IBNJAWZI-ZAD(ابن عباس); RAZI-FULL; DURR(ابن عباس); DURR-FULL(ابن عباس); TABATABAI; SAMARRAI-LAMASAT]
- 1:7/q04/p4 The Prophet's Companions — MAWARDI-FULL reporting عبد الرحمن بن زيد: He identifies those favored as Muhammad and the Companions with him. IBNATIYYA reporting الحسن بن أبي الحسن: Al-Ḥasan identifies the favored people as the Companions of Muḥammad. IBNATIYYA-FULL reporting الحسن بن أبي الحسن: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan identifies the favored as the Companions of Muhammad. BAYDAWI: Another interpretation identifies those blessed with the Prophet Muhammad and his companions. ABUHAYYAN reporting الحسن: Al-Hasan identifies those favored as the Companions of the Prophet. ABUHAYYAN-FULL reporting الحسن: Al-Ḥasan identifies the favored people as the Companions of Muḥammad. ALUSI reporting قيل: Another view identifies those blessed as the Companions of Muḥammad. STUDYQURAN: Those God blessed are identified in 4:69 as prophets, truthful ones, witnesses, and righteous people, excellent companions. | mentions 4:69 [8 notes: MAWARDI-FULL(عبد الرحمن بن زيد); IBNATIYYA(الحسن بن أبي الحسن); IBNATIYYA-FULL(الحسن بن أبي الحسن); BAYDAWI; ABUHAYYAN(الحسن); ABUHAYYAN-FULL(الحسن); ALUSI(قيل); STUDYQURAN]
- 1:7/q04/p5 Faithful followers of Moses and Jesus before their religion changed — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting ابن عباس: Ibn ʿAbbās says those given favor were the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's blessings. WAHIDI-QT: Those favored with guidance are the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favor. WAHIDI-WAJIZ: Those granted favor are the followers of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favor. KASHSHAF-FULL reporting ابن عباس: Ibn Abbas identifies those blessed as Moses's companions before they changed their religion; another view identifies them as prophets. IBNATIYYA-FULL reporting فرقة من المفسرين: A group of exegetes says the favored are the believers among the Children of Israel, citing God's address to Israel in 2:40, 2:47, and 2:122. | mentions 2:40, 2:47, 2:122 IBNATIYYA-FULL reporting ابن عباس: Ibn ʿAbbas also identifies the favored as Moses' followers before they changed their religion; the author says this matches the previous interpretation. BAYDAWI-FULL: The favored are variously identified as prophets; the Prophet and his Companions; or the uncorrupted, un-abrogated followers of Moses and Jesus. NASAFI-FULL: Those favored are the believers and prophets, or the people of Moses before they changed. ABUHAYYAN: Among the proposed referents of those favored are prophets, angels, and the unaltered communities of Moses and Jesus; Abū Ḥayyān lists these as alternatives rather than restricting the wording to one group. ABUHAYYAN reporting فرقة: One group identifies those favored as the believers among the Children of Israel. - 1:7/q04/p6 Prophets and believers — IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB: Those granted favor on the straight path are the prophets and believers. THALABI: The phrase is an appositive to the first ṣirāṭ: those favored are guided and cared for in affirmation of divine unity; the author identifies them as prophets and believers and cites 4:69. | mentions 4:69 ABUHAYYAN-FULL reporting وكيع: Wakīʿ identifies those favored as prophets and believers, or as Muslims. ## 1:7/q05 What does 'bestowed favor' mean in Arabic?  [أَنْعَمْتَ · meaning]
- 1:7/q05/p1 Niʿma originally conveys increase or doing something thoroughly; the usage أنعما for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar means they surpassed others in good. — THALABI: Niʿma originally conveys increase or doing something thoroughly; the usage أنعما for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar means they surpassed others in good. [1 notes: THALABI]
- 1:7/q05/p2 In the verse, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim means the road of those on whom You bestowed favor; the clause could describe an indefinite qawm directly, but not a definite group. — WAHIDI-BASIT: In the verse, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim means the road of those on whom You bestowed favor; the clause could describe an indefinite qawm directly, but not a definite group. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q05/p3 Inʿām, iḥsān, and ifḍāl are near-synonyms, though one may act beneficently toward oneself but cannot bless oneself; niʿma derives from softness and denotes good intended benefit. — JISHUMI: Inʿām, iḥsān, and ifḍāl are near-synonyms, though one may act beneficently toward oneself but cannot bless oneself; niʿma derives from softness and denotes good intended benefit. [1 notes: JISHUMI]
- 1:7/q05/p4 The root of niʿma carries the sense of intensification or addition, as in grinding medicine thoroughly. — TABRISI: The root of niʿma carries the sense of intensification or addition, as in grinding medicine thoroughly. [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q05/p5 One definition makes a blessing a benefit bestowed as kindness upon another. — RAZI-FULL reporting بعضهم: One definition makes a blessing a benefit bestowed as kindness upon another. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL(بعضهم)]
- 1:7/q05/p6 A pure harm is not a blessing, because the definition requires a benefit. — RAZI-FULL: A pure harm is not a blessing, because the definition requires a benefit. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q05/p7 The verse means asking for the path of those favored; 4:69 identifies them as prophets and the truthful, whose chief is Abu Bakr, so it supports his imamate and the propriety of following him.; cited verses: 4:69 — RAZI-FULL: The verse means asking for the path of those favored; 4:69 identifies them as prophets and the truthful, whose chief is Abu Bakr, so it supports his imamate and the propriety of following him. | mentions 4:69 [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q05/p8 The favor cannot mean worldly benefits; it means religious favor, and among these faith alone can exist without the other religious gifts. — RAZI-FULL: The favor cannot mean worldly benefits; it means religious favor, and among these faith alone can exist without the other religious gifts. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q05/p9 Ahmad means the greatest of those praising, and greater praise follows from greater blessing; Muhammad therefore received exceptional mercy and is mercy to all worlds.; cited verses: 21:107 — RAZI-FULL: Ahmad means the greatest of those praising, and greater praise follows from greater blessing; Muhammad therefore received exceptional mercy and is mercy to all worlds. | mentions 21:107 [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q05/p10 Inʿām means conveying a blessing; niʿma originally denotes a pleasing state and is extended to what is enjoyed as blessing. — BAYDAWI: Inʿām means conveying a blessing; niʿma originally denotes a pleasing state and is extended to what is enjoyed as blessing. [1 notes: BAYDAWI]
- 1:7/q05/p11 Niʿma denotes ease and softness of living; the south wind and ostrich are also named from softness, and anʿama ʿalayhi means to bestow abundantly. — ABUHAYYAN: Niʿma denotes ease and softness of living; the south wind and ostrich are also named from softness, and anʿama ʿalayhi means to bestow abundantly. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q05/p12 Anʿama illustrates one of the twenty-four meanings of form IV, making its object a possessor of the root's meaning, here a blessing. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: Anʿama illustrates one of the twenty-four meanings of form IV, making its object a possessor of the root's meaning, here a blessing. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q05/p13 The appositional restatement confirms that the straight way comes only through God's favor and signals that clinging to it means following His messengers. — BIQAI: The appositional restatement confirms that the straight way comes only through God's favor and signals that clinging to it means following His messengers. [1 notes: BIQAI]
- 1:7/q05/p14 Using غير rather than an exception marks exclusion from the outset, making clear that the requested universal blessing means the special honor granted to the faithful, not the general gift of existence. — BIQAI-FULL: Using غير rather than an exception marks exclusion from the outset, making clear that the requested universal blessing means the special honor granted to the faithful, not the general gift of existence. [1 notes: BIQAI-FULL]
- 1:7/q05/p15 Al-Fatiha's final prayer details the highest request: faith protected from sin and its resulting wrath and error; “those You favored” means believers, and the favor is unrestricted because faith entails every blessing. — ITQAN: Al-Fatiha's final prayer details the highest request: faith protected from sin and its resulting wrath and error; “those You favored” means believers, and the favor is unrestricted because faith entails every blessing. [1 notes: ITQAN]
- 1:7/q05/p16 Those You favored is a complete substitution for the first straight path; favor here means the religion's beneficial gift. — BURSEVI: Those You favored is a complete substitution for the first straight path; favor here means the religion's beneficial gift. [1 notes: BURSEVI]
- 1:7/q05/p17 A reported definition calls a blessing a benefit given by someone superior to a person without compensation. — ALUSI reporting قيل: A reported definition calls a blessing a benefit given by someone superior to a person without compensation. [1 notes: ALUSI(قيل)]
- 1:7/q05/p18 Their existence is certain, and asking for their path proceeds from that certainty; their specific members can be identified mentally according to what blessing means. — ELMALILI: Their existence is certain, and asking for their path proceeds from that certainty; their specific members can be identified mentally according to what blessing means. [1 notes: ELMALILI]
- 1:7/q05/p19 Receiving the route or means to a blessing secures repeated access to it, unlike receiving a single instance of the blessing. — ELMALILI: Receiving the route or means to a blessing secures repeated access to it, unlike receiving a single instance of the blessing. [1 notes: ELMALILI]
- 1:7/q05/p20 Asking to join the favored in rank also implies emulating the means by which they rose; it prepares disavowal of the other groups with hope and seeking refuge.; cited verses: 60:6 — IBNASHUR: Asking to join the favored in rank also implies emulating the means by which they rose; it prepares disavowal of the other groups with hope and seeking refuge. | mentions 60:6 [1 notes: IBNASHUR]
- 1:7/q05/p21 Niʿma derives from naʿīm, comfort, ease of living, what suits a person, and luxury; its verb has the patterns of samiʿa, naṣara, and ḍaraba. — IBNASHUR: Niʿma derives from naʿīm, comfort, ease of living, what suits a person, and luxury; its verb has the patterns of samiʿa, naṣara, and ḍaraba. [1 notes: IBNASHUR]
- 1:7/q05/p22 Whether the favored means prophets, their best followers, or earlier Muslims, the request is for a complete path suited to guidance available in each age. — IBNASHUR: Whether the favored means prophets, their best followers, or earlier Muslims, the request is for a complete path suited to guidance available in each age. [1 notes: IBNASHUR]
- 1:7/q05/p23 Niʿma derives from ease and pleasant living; the feminine noun denotes a good state, first bodily pleasure and later beneficial intellectual or spiritual goods. — IBNASHUR-FULL: Niʿma derives from ease and pleasant living; the feminine noun denotes a good state, first bodily pleasure and later beneficial intellectual or spiritual goods. [1 notes: IBNASHUR-FULL]

## 1:7/q06 What favor was bestowed on them?  [أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ · interpretation]
- 1:7/q06/p1 Those granted favor are the prophets, whom God favored with prophethood.; cited verses: 19:58 — MUQATIL: Those granted favor are the prophets, whom God favored with prophethood. | mentions 19:58 [1 notes: MUQATIL]
- 1:7/q06/p2 The two genitive parses are close in meaning: those favored with true guidance are not under God's wrath or astray; the adjectival parse states this directly. — TAB: The two genitive parses are close in meaning: those favored with true guidance are not under God's wrath or astray; the adjectival parse states this directly. [1 notes: TAB]
- 1:7/q06/p3 Obedience and guidance come to the obedient only through God's favor and enabling; the verse attributes their guidance, worship, and obedience to His beneficence. — TAB: Obedience and guidance come to the obedient only through God's favor and enabling; the verse attributes their guidance, worship, and obedience to His beneficence. [1 notes: TAB]
- 1:7/q06/p4 The verse leaves the blessing unstated because the nearby phrase already makes clear that the blessing is guidance to the upright path; Arabic can omit what context supplies. — TAB: The verse leaves the blessing unstated because the nearby phrase already makes clear that the blessing is guidance to the upright path; Arabic can omit what context supplies. [1 notes: TAB]
- 1:7/q06/p5 The requested guidance is to the path God described; whoever follows it obediently will be brought to the company and dwelling of those favored, and God never breaks His promise.; cited verses: 4:69 — TAB-FULL: The requested guidance is to the path God described; whoever follows it obediently will be brought to the company and dwelling of those favored, and God never breaks His promise. | mentions 4:69 [1 notes: TAB-FULL]
- 1:7/q06/p6 The two genitive parses have nearly the same implication: those truly favored with guidance to the true religion are not under God's anger and are not astray. — TAB-FULL: The two genitive parses have nearly the same implication: those truly favored with guidance to the true religion are not under God's anger and are not astray. [1 notes: TAB-FULL]
- 1:7/q06/p7 God's favor includes teaching them the path's dangers, Satan's tricks, and the ego's treachery. — SULAMI reporting أبو عثمان: God's favor includes teaching them the path's dangers, Satan's tricks, and the ego's treachery. [1 notes: SULAMI(أبو عثمان)]
- 1:7/q06/p8 The favor consists of faith, guidance, enabling, care, watchfulness, and protection. — SULAMI reporting بعضهم: The favor consists of faith, guidance, enabling, care, watchfulness, and protection. [1 notes: SULAMI(بعضهم)]
- 1:7/q06/p9 God's favor includes granting permission to converse with and petition Him. — SULAMI reporting بعضهم: God's favor includes granting permission to converse with and petition Him. [1 notes: SULAMI(بعضهم)]
- 1:7/q06/p10 Those favored with this path are saints and the elect, whom God has annihilated from themselves and established through Himself, without hidden divine stratagems stopping them. — QUSHAYRI: Those favored with this path are saints and the elect, whom God has annihilated from themselves and established through Himself, without hidden divine stratagems stopping them. [1 notes: QUSHAYRI]
- 1:7/q06/p11 Ibn Jarīr says the verse is elliptical: guide us along the path of those You favored with guidance to the path, since Arabic omits words when context supplies them. — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting محمد بن جرير: Ibn Jarīr says the verse is elliptical: guide us along the path of those You favored with guidance to the path, since Arabic omits words when context supplies them. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT(محمد بن جرير)]
- 1:7/q06/p12 In the verse, ghayr al-maghḍūb describes the favored people and is definite because one favored with faith is not under wrath. — WAHIDI-BASIT: In the verse, ghayr al-maghḍūb describes the favored people and is definite because one favored with faith is not under wrath. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q06/p13 Those favored with guidance are the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favor. — WAHIDI-QT: Those favored with guidance are the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favor. [1 notes: WAHIDI-QT]
- 1:7/q06/p14 Niʿmah can mean prophethood, as in the people favored with prophecy.; cited verses: 4:69, 93:11 — DAMGHANI: Niʿmah can mean prophethood, as in the people favored with prophecy. | mentions 4:69, 93:11 [1 notes: DAMGHANI]
- 1:7/q06/p15 Another view includes everyone God kept firm in faith among the prophets and believers, as in the verse about those favored alongside the prophets.; cited verses: 4:69 — BAGHAWI: Another view includes everyone God kept firm in faith among the prophets and believers, as in the verse about those favored alongside the prophets. | mentions 4:69 [1 notes: BAGHAWI]
- 1:7/q06/p16 The blessing is general to include every blessing; whoever receives Islam receives every blessing. — KASHSHAF: The blessing is general to include every blessing; whoever receives Islam receives every blessing. [1 notes: KASHSHAF]
- 1:7/q06/p17 Because God is explicitly the giver of faith, He creates and grants it; otherwise the servant would bestow the greatest blessing and God's praise of His own favor would be misplaced, against the Mu'tazilites. — RAZI-FULL: Because God is explicitly the giver of faith, He creates and grants it; otherwise the servant would bestow the greatest blessing and God's praise of His own favor would be misplaced, against the Mu'tazilites. - 1:7/q06/p18 God is not obligated to provide the best religious guidance: a required act would not count as a favor, whereas the verse calls it one. — RAZI-FULL: God is not obligated to provide the best religious guidance: a required act would not count as a favor, whereas the verse calls it one. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q06/p19 The seven Fatiha verses remove seven vices: praise dispels desire, Lord of the worlds greed, Judgment Day anger, worship and aid pride and vanity, guidance caprice, the favored path unbelief and doubt, and the final phrase innovation. — RAZI-FULL: The seven Fatiha verses remove seven vices: praise dispels desire, Lord of the worlds greed, Judgment Day anger, worship and aid pride and vanity, guidance caprice, the favored path unbelief and doubt, and the final phrase innovation. - 1:7/q06/p21 The intended favor is the final afterlife good and whatever leads to it, including forgiveness, divine approval, and residence in the highest ranks; other favors are shared with unbelievers. — BAYDAWI-FULL: The intended favor is the final afterlife good and whatever leads to it, including forgiveness, divine approval, and residence in the highest ranks; other favors are shared with unbelievers. - 1:7/q06/p23 The explanation of inward and outward blessing is linked to 31:20, which says God has poured out both manifest and hidden blessings upon you.; cited verses: 31:20 — ABUHAYYAN: The explanation of inward and outward blessing is linked to 31:20, which says God has poured out both manifest and hidden blessings upon you. | mentions 31:20 [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q06/p24 The prayer asks that guidance to the path of the favored continue: those who praise God and declare worship and reliance already possess guidance, but ask for its permanence. — ABUHAYYAN: The prayer asks that guidance to the path of the favored continue: those who praise God and declare worship and reliance already possess guidance, but ask for its permanence. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q06/p25 Anger precedes misguidance in the wording although it results from it because it contrasts with favor: favor brings good and requital brings harm; the order also suits the sūra's cadence. — ABUHAYYAN: Anger precedes misguidance in the wording although it results from it because it contrasts with favor: favor brings good and requital brings harm; the order also suits the sūra's cadence. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN]
- 1:7/q06/p26 This apposition restates the request for guidance, making it firmer and more emphatic by directing it to the path of those God favored. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: This apposition restates the request for guidance, making it firmer and more emphatic by directing it to the path of those God favored. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q06/p27 The intended favor is religious; “those angered” and “those astray” are general categories of everyone who incurs anger and goes astray. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: The intended favor is religious; “those angered” and “those astray” are general categories of everyone who incurs anger and goes astray. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q06/p28 Anger precedes misguidance despite resulting from it because it is paired antithetically with favor; the order also suits the verse-ending cadence and the conjunction itself implies no sequence. — ABUHAYYAN-FULL: Anger precedes misguidance despite resulting from it because it is paired antithetically with favor; the order also suits the verse-ending cadence and the conjunction itself implies no sequence. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]
- 1:7/q06/p29 One explanation says praise uses third person because it ranks below worship, while direct address elevates the worshipper's encounter; similarly, blessing is explicitly attributed to God but anger is phrased obliquely as a matter of etiquette.; cited… — BURHAN reporting قيل: One explanation says praise uses third person because it ranks below worship, while direct address elevates the worshipper's encounter; similarly, blessing is explicitly attributed to God but anger is phrased obliquely as a matter of etiquette. | mentions 6:101 [1 notes: BURHAN(قيل)]
- 1:7/q06/p30 The following disavowal specifies that the requested blessing is not merely worldly, asking refuge from those wandering in confusion or injustice. — BIQAI: The following disavowal specifies that the requested blessing is not merely worldly, asking refuge from those wandering in confusion or injustice. - 1:7/q06/p31 Since existence itself is a blessing and everyone follows some human path, the request must mean those specially favored with God's mercy, whose opposites are then identified as a warning. — BIQAI: Since existence itself is a blessing and everyone follows some human path, the request must mean those specially favored with God's mercy, whose opposites are then identified as a warning. [1 notes: BIQAI]
- 1:7/q06/p32 Mentioning these groups after hope inspires fear alongside hope and clarifies that the intended blessing is the special grace given to the honored. — BIQAI: Mentioning these groups after hope inspires fear alongside hope and clarifies that the intended blessing is the special grace given to the honored. [1 notes: BIQAI]
- 1:7/q06/p33 In Qatada's sequential gloss, the Day of Recompense is when creatures are repaid; the worship-prayer is what people should say and directs them to God; the straight path is named, the favored are prophets, the objects of… — DURR reporting قتادة: In Qatada's sequential gloss, the Day of Recompense is when creatures are repaid; the worship-prayer is what people should say and directs them to God; the straight path is named, the favored are prophets, the objects of anger are Jews, and the astray are Christians. - 1:7/q06/p34 Those granted favor are prophets and believers whom God favored with Islam and prophethood. — DURR-FULL reporting ابن عباس: Those granted favor are prophets and believers whom God favored with Islam and prophethood. [1 notes: DURR-FULL(ابن عباس)]
- 1:7/q06/p35 Al-Fatiha's final prayer details the highest request: faith protected from sin and its resulting wrath and error; “those You favored” means believers, and the favor is unrestricted because faith entails every blessing. — ITQAN: Al-Fatiha's final prayer details the highest request: faith protected from sin and its resulting wrath and error; “those You favored” means believers, and the favor is unrestricted because faith entails every blessing. [1 notes: ALUSI]
- 1:7/q06/p37 Divine favor is conveying benefit to rational beings; hence one does not say that God favored a horse, and the blessing is defined as an unmotivated benefit to a human. — ALUSI-FULL: Divine favor is conveying benefit to rational beings; hence one does not say that God favored a horse, and the blessing is defined as an unmotivated benefit to a human. ## 1:7/q07 Does God bestow favor on unbelievers?  [أَنْعَمْتَ · theology]
- 1:7/q07/p1 God blesses both believers and unbelievers; His first favor to a servant is creating that person alive for benefit. — JISHUMI: God blesses both believers and unbelievers; His first favor to a servant is creating that person alive for benefit. [1 notes: JISHUMI]
- 1:7/q07/p2 Some of Razi's Ash'arite colleagues deny that God bestows any blessing on unbelievers. — RAZI-FULL reporting أصحابنا: Some of Razi's Ash'arite colleagues deny that God bestows any blessing on unbelievers. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL(أصحابنا)]
- 1:7/q07/p3 The Mu'tazilites affirm that God gives unbelievers both religious and worldly blessings. — RAZI-FULL reporting المعتزلة: The Mu'tazilites affirm that God gives unbelievers both religious and worldly blessings. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL(المعتزلة)]
- 1:7/q07/p4 Razi supports his colleagues: if unbelievers were among those favored, asking for the favored path would ask for their path; calling the phrase appositional to the straight path does not remove that consequence. — RAZI-FULL: Razi supports his colleagues: if unbelievers were among those favored, asking for the favored path would ask for their path; calling the phrase appositional to the straight path does not remove that consequence. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL+]
- 1:7/q07/p5 Razi also cites the verse saying unbelievers' respite increases their sin as evidence against calling their worldly lot a blessing.; cited verses: 3:178 — RAZI-FULL: Razi also cites the verse saying unbelievers' respite increases their sin as evidence against calling their worldly lot a blessing. | mentions 3:178 [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q07/p6 They also cite God's bringing people to life as an act of grace, His reminder to Israel of His favor, and statements that few give thanks as evidence that blessings reach unbelievers.; cited verses: 2:28, 2:40, 34:13,… — RAZI-FULL reporting المعتزلة: They also cite God's bringing people to life as an act of grace, His reminder to Israel of His favor, and statements that few give thanks as evidence that blessings reach unbelievers. | mentions 2:28, 2:40, 34:13, 7:17 [1 notes: RAZI-FULL(المعتزلة)]
- 1:7/q07/p7 The verse divides people into the obedient who are favored, sinners under wrath, and those ignorant of religion or unbelievers who are astray. — RAZI-FULL: The verse divides people into the obedient who are favored, sinners under wrath, and those ignorant of religion or unbelievers who are astray. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q07/p8 The clause about those God favored reveals the ranks of the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous; the next clauses disclose the ranks of sinners and unbelievers. — RAZI-FULL: The clause about those God favored reveals the ranks of the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous; the next clauses disclose the ranks of sinners and unbelievers. [1 notes: RAZI-FULL]
- 1:7/q07/p9 The verse primarily intends the final, otherworldly blessing and what leads to it, since other blessings are shared by believers and unbelievers. — BAYDAWI: The verse primarily intends the final, otherworldly blessing and what leads to it, since other blessings are shared by believers and unbelievers. [1 notes: BAYDAWI]

## 1:7/q08 Who grants faith, guidance, and obedience?  [أَنْعَمْتَ · theology]
- 1:7/q08/p1 The two genitive parses are close in meaning: those favored with true guidance are not under God's wrath or astray; the adjectival parse states this directly. — TAB: The two genitive parses are close in meaning: those favored with true guidance are not under God's wrath or astray; the adjectival parse states this directly. ## 1:7/q09 Is the object of God's favor omitted, and why?  [أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ · grammar]

[1 notes: SAMARRAI-LAMASAT]

- 1:7/q10/p20 The sole Quranic attribution of blessing to someone besides God occurs when the Prophet’s special favor to Zayd is mentioned after God’s favor to him.; cited verses: 33:37 — SAMARRAI-LAMASAT: The sole Quranic attribution of blessing to someone besides God occurs when the Prophet’s special favor to Zayd is mentioned after God’s favor to him. | mentions 33:37 [1 notes: SAMARRAI-LAMASAT]

## 1:7/q11 What are the syntax and senses of 'upon' and its pronoun?  [عَلَيْهِمْ · grammar]
- 1:7/q11/p1 The two pronunciations of the pronoun in ʿalayhim are both Arabic dialects. — FARRA: The two pronunciations of the pronoun in ʿalayhim are both Arabic dialects. [1 notes: FARRA]
- 1:7/q11/p2 Genitive ghayri is an adjective of alladhīna, not of the pronoun in ʿalayhim; its definite annexation permits this description because neither expression denotes a specified person. — FARRA: Genitive ghayri is an adjective of alladhīna, not of the pronoun in ʿalayhim; its definite annexation permits this description because neither expression denotes a specified person. [1 notes: FARRA]
- 1:7/q11/p3 Ghayri can be accusative as a detached description of ʿalayhim, or genitive after repeating ṣirāṭ as “the path of those other than …”. — FARRA: Ghayri can be accusative as a detached description of ʿalayhim, or genitive after repeating ṣirāṭ as “the path of those other than …”. [1 notes: FARRA]
- 1:7/q11/p4 Ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim is accusative as an appositive to al-ṣirāṭ. — AKHFASH: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim is accusative as an appositive to al-ṣirāṭ. [1 notes: AKHFASH]
- 1:7/q11/p5 The possible accusative parse treats ghayr as a detached adjective of the pronoun in ʿalayhim, which is syntactically governed by anʿamta. — TAB: The possible accusative parse treats ghayr as a detached adjective of the pronoun in ʿalayhim, which is syntactically governed by anʿamta. [1 notes: TAB]
- 1:7/q11/p6 Anʿamta ʿalayhim is the relative clause, and its pronoun refers back to alladhīna. — NAHHAS: Anʿamta ʿalayhim is the relative clause, and its pronoun refers back to alladhīna. [1 notes: NAHHAS]
- 1:7/q11/p7 Ibn Kaysān permits ghayr al-maghḍūbi as an adjective or apposition to alladhīna, and also as apposition to their pronoun in ʿalayhim. — NAHHAS reporting ابن كيسان: Ibn Kaysān permits ghayr al-maghḍūbi as an adjective or apposition to alladhīna, and also as apposition to their pronoun in ʿalayhim. [1 notes: NAHHAS(ابن كيسان)]
- 1:7/q11/p8 They preserve kasra on hāʾ because it is the same pronoun hāʾ as in ʿalayhi and its cause for kasra remains unchanged after mim is added. — FARISI-HUJJA reporting عاصم وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن عامر: They preserve kasra on hāʾ because it is the same pronoun hāʾ as in ʿalayhi and its cause for kasra remains unchanged after mim is added. [1 notes: FARISI-HUJJA(عاصم وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن عامر)]
- 1:7/q11/p9 Pronoun hāʾ’s hiddenness is shown by movements inserted before it in pause, and by their disappearance in liaison when hāʾ itself makes the vowel clear. — FARISI-HUJJA reporting أبو علي: Pronoun hāʾ’s hiddenness is shown by movements inserted before it in pause, and by their disappearance in liaison when hāʾ itself makes the vowel clear. [1 notes: FARISI-HUJJA(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q11/p10 The phrase اشتر لنا سويقا can be explained by treating the liaison as pause, among the analyses of movement before pronoun hāʾ. — FARISI-HUJJA reporting أبو علي: The phrase اشتر لنا سويقا can be explained by treating the liaison as pause, among the analyses of movement before pronoun hāʾ. [1 notes: FARISI-HUJJA(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q11/p11 An objection says damma is the default for genitive pronoun hāʾ, as its accusative counterpart is damma and damma works in more environments than kasra. — FARISI-HUJJA reporting أبو علي: An objection says damma is the default for genitive pronoun hāʾ, as its accusative counterpart is damma and damma works in more environments than kasra. [1 notes: FARISI-HUJJA(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q11/p12 Plural mim always follows a kasra or damma, both heavy, unlike singular pronoun hāʾ, which can follow fatha or sukūn; this licenses still mim. — FARISI-HUJJA reporting أبو علي: Plural mim always follows a kasra or damma, both heavy, unlike singular pronoun hāʾ, which can follow fatha or sukūn; this licenses still mim. [1 notes: FARISI-HUJJA(أبو علي)]
- 1:7/q11/p13 The hāʾ in ʿalayhim may be pronounced with either kasra or ḍamma; kasra follows because yāʾ is related to kasra and the lighter transition is preferred. — WAHIDI-BASIT: The hāʾ in ʿalayhim may be pronounced with either kasra or ḍamma; kasra follows because yāʾ is related to kasra and the lighter transition is preferred. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT]
- 1:7/q11/p14 Warsh from Nāfiʿ pronounces plural mīm with ḍamma and links a following initial hamza with wāw; dropping hamza and moving its vowel requires the mīm to recover its original ḍamma and lengthen. — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting ورش عن نافع: Warsh from Nāfiʿ pronounces plural mīm with ḍamma and links a following initial hamza with wāw; dropping hamza and moving its vowel requires the mīm to recover its original ḍamma and lengthen. [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT(ورش عن نافع)]
- 1:7/q11/p15 The author of al-Ḥujja says genitive ghayr is either apposition or adjective; apposition implies repeating the governing factor, as the repeated prepositions in 7:75 show.; cited verses: 7:75 — WAHIDI-BASIT reporting صاحب الحجة: The author of al-Ḥujja says genitive ghayr is either apposition or adjective; apposition implies repeating the governing factor, as the repeated prepositions in 7:75 show. | mentions 7:75 [1 notes: WAHIDI-BASIT(صاحب الحجة)]
- 1:7/q11/p16 In al-Fātiḥa, ṣirāṭ is the object, al-mustaqīm its adjective, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim apposes the preceding phrase, and the remaining clauses modify or coordinate with it. — JURJANI-DALAIL: In al-Fātiḥa, ṣirāṭ is the object, al-mustaqīm its adjective, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim apposes the preceding phrase, and the remaining clauses modify or coordinate with it. [1 notes: JURJANI-DALAIL]
- 1:7/q11/p17 Hamza pronounces the hāʾ in ʿalayhim, ladayhim, and ilayhim with ḍamma. — BAGHAWI reporting حمزة: Hamza pronounces the hāʾ in ʿalayhim, ladayhim, and ilayhim with ḍamma. [1 notes: BAGHAWI(حمزة)]
- 1:7/q11/p18 The first ʿalayhim is accusative as object of anʿamta; the second is nominative as agent in the passive phrase. — KASHSHAF: The first ʿalayhim is accusative as object of anʿamta; the second is nominative as agent in the passive phrase. [1 notes: KASHSHAF]
- 1:7/q11/p19 Alladhīna is a relative noun, and anʿamta ʿalayhim is its relative clause; together they form a genitive noun annexed to ṣirāṭ. — TABRISI: Alladhīna is a relative noun, and anʿamta ʿalayhim is its relative clause; together they form a genitive noun annexed to ṣirāṭ. [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q11/p20 In the genitive, ghayr may be an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim or to alladhīna, or an adjective of the relative phrase despite ghayr usually modifying an indefinite noun. — TABRISI: In the genitive, ghayr may be an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim or to alladhīna, or an adjective of the relative phrase despite ghayr usually modifying an indefinite noun. [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q11/p21 The word maghdūb need not be pluralized because the plural pronoun in ʿalayhim already marks those who incur anger. — TABRISI: The word maghdūb need not be pluralized because the plural pronoun in ʿalayhim already marks those who incur anger. [1 notes: TABRISI]
- 1:7/q11/p22 Hamza pronounces the hā in ʿalayhim and its parallels with ḍamma and the mīm quiescent; Yaqub uses ḍamma on hā preceded by a silent yā in duals and masculine and feminine plurals. — TABRISI reporting حمزة ويعقوب: Hamza pronounces the hā in ʿalayhim and its parallels with ḍamma and the mīm quiescent; Yaqub uses ḍamma on hā preceded by a silent yā in duals and masculine and feminine plurals. [1 notes: TABRISI(حمزة ويعقوب)]
- 1:7/q11/p23 Most readers pronounce the pronoun in ʿalayhim with kasra, as in ladayhim and ilayhim. — IBNJAWZI-ZAD reporting الأكثرون: Most readers pronounce the pronoun in ʿalayhim with kasra, as in ladayhim and ilayhim. [1 notes: IBNJAWZI-ZAD(الأكثرون)]
- 1:7/q11/p24 Alayhim is grammatically nominative in sense because the underlying construction is “wrath came upon them.” — QURTUBI: Alayhim is grammatically nominative in sense because the underlying construction is “wrath came upon them.” [1 notes: QURTUBI]
- 1:7/q11/p25 The genitive may make ghayr an appositive to alladhina or to the pronoun in alayhim, or an adjective; although definite nouns usually are not modified by indefinite ones, alladhina is general here or ghayr is definite between… — QURTUBI-FULL: The genitive may make ghayr an appositive to alladhina or to the pronoun in alayhim, or an adjective; although definite nouns usually are not modified by indefinite ones, alladhina is general here or ghayr is definite between exclusive opposites. [1 notes: QURTUBI-FULL]
- 1:7/q11/p26 Ibn Kathīr reads ghayr in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in ʿalayhim, governed by anʿamta. — BAYDAWI reporting ابن كثير: Ibn Kathīr reads ghayr in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in ʿalayhim, governed by anʿamta. - 1:7/q11/p28 The first ‘upon them’ is in the accusative position as an object, while the second is in the nominative position as a subject. — NASAFI: The first ‘upon them’ is in the accusative position as an object, while the second is in the nominative position as a subject. [1 notes: NASAFI]
- 1:7/q11/p29 The first “upon them” is an object and the second is a subject; God's anger means His will to exact revenge and impose punishment on deniers. — NASAFI-FULL: The first “upon them” is an object and the second is a subject; God's anger means His will to exact revenge and impose punishment on deniers. - 1:7/q11/p30 The prepositional phrase عليهم is in the accusative position because it is governed by an active verb; the same applies to a preposition governed by a non-passive verb or equivalent. — ABUHAYYAN: The prepositional phrase عليهم is in the accusative position because it is governed by an active verb; the same applies to a preposition governed by a non-passive verb or equivalent. [1 notes: ABUHAYYAN-FULL]

[1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]

- 1:7/q11/p40 ʿAlā can be a noun meaning above when preceded by a preposition, and may be nominal where treating it as a preposition would produce an impermissible link between detached and attached pronouns. — SAMIN-DURR: ʿAlā can be a noun meaning above when preceded by a preposition, and may be nominal where treating it as a preposition would produce an impermissible link between detached and attached pronouns. [1 notes: SAMIN-DURR(مكي)]

[1 notes: SAMIN-DURR]
